xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DisclosureOfNotesOnFinancialRe:
1. The above results were reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors at its meeting held on November 04, 2026 and were subjected to review by the Statutory Auditors.

2. The Group had received a settlement offer during the previous year from Beste Motor Co. Ltd. and TYC Brother Industrial Co. Ltd. (“TYC Parties”) alleging breach of Transition Management Agreement (‘TMA’ or ‘agreement’) in respect of certain income amounting to Rs. 209.89 million recognised during the quarter ended June 30, 2025 and Rs. 231.82 million recognised during the year ended March 31, 2025 by the Group under ‘Revenue from operations’, as received from Chongqing Varroc TYC Auto Lamps Co., Ltd. (erstwhile joint venture). Subsequently, the Group received Statement of Claim under the arbitration proceedings originally initiated by TYC Parties in August 2022, on the aforesaid matter and on certain additional claims/breaches under the aforesaid TMA, which are to be quantified against which the Group has filed Statement of defence in March 2026. The Group believes that it has a strong case and will take appropriate actions as necessary to protect its interests. The auditors in their review report have included a qualification in respect of this matter.

3. Exceptional items for the periods presented in the consolidated financial results include the following:

a. On September 30, 2026, the Group announced a proposed restructuring of its operations in Italy involving discontinuation of the manufacturing, laboratory and testing activities of Varroc Italy S.p.A. ('Varroc Italy'), while continuing with certain sales and research and development activities in Italy. The restructuring has been initiated in view of the continued losses and high operating costs of the subsidiary. Pursuant to the restructuring plan, the Group has recognised a provision of Eur 4.48 million (Rs. 493.87 million) for obligations directly attributable to the restructuring, mainly comprising costs associated with the transfer/disposal of plant and machinery and other related expenses. The resulting charge of Rs. 493.87 million has been disclosed as an exceptional item in the consolidated financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.

4. The Holding Company made the following Commercial Paper (CP) issuances:
a) 1,000 listed unsecured Commercial Papers (CPs) of face value Rs. 5,00,000 aggregating to Rs. 500 million and having interest rate of 7.2% were issued on July 22, 2026, and redeemed on August 21, 2026.
b) 1,000 listed unsecured Commercial Papers (CPs) of face value Rs. 5,00,000 aggregating to Rs. 500 million and having interest rate of 6.90% were issued on September 24, 2026 and are due for redemption on December 23, 2026.

5. Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Holding Company entered into an agreement to acquire 45% stake in Forsee Power India Private Limited for an initial consideration of Eur 4.50 million, with a right to acquire an additional 6% stake and contingent consideration of up to Eur 2.00 million. The transaction, with maximum consideration of Eur 6.50 million, is subject to applicable approvals.

6. The 'Automotive' segment consists of the business of automobile products consisting of auto parts for two-wheelers, three-wheelers and four-wheelers and related design, development and engineering activities and other services. 'Others' comprise of forging components for off road vehicles and components for mining and oil drilling industry which is below the thresholds for reporting as separate operating segment. Investment in joint ventures and corresponding share of profit/loss from joint ventures is considered under unallocated assets and profit/loss respectively.
